questions.stem: 提示：網路購物越來越方便，隨時都能下單，商品還會直接送到家門口；但街上仍有許多實體商店，讓顧客可以親手挑選。請仔細觀察下面兩張圖，寫一篇英文作文，文分兩段。第一段比較圖一實體店與圖二網路購物兩種購物情境的不同；第二段評估這兩種購物方式對消費者的利弊，並提出一個讓自己成為更聰明消費者的具體做法。

1.explanation_zh: 這一題有三個要求：第一段比較兩種購物情境；第二段評估兩種購物方式對消費者的利弊，再提出讓自己成為更聰明消費者的具體做法。第一段可以從圖中找比較點：能不能試穿與詢問店員、購物的時間與地點、和人互動或一個人滑手機。第二段的做法要具體（例如「放進購物車一天後再決定」），只寫「要理性消費」太空泛。
evidence: 比較圖一實體店與圖二網路購物兩種購物情境的不同
評估這兩種購物方式對消費者的利弊
提出一個讓自己成為更聰明消費者的具體做法
1.strategy_zh: 用一次衝動購物的經驗把「網購的缺點」和「自己的做法」串起來；做法寫成一兩條能執行的規則，並說明效果。
hints: 第一段：用 while、in contrast 逐點比較試穿、時間與互動
第二段前半：兩種方式各寫一個好處與一個壞處，可以用自己的購物經驗支持
第二段後半：提出自己的消費規則，說明效果並寫出見解

content.focus_zh: 第一段要逐點比較兩種購物情境（能不能試穿與詢問、購物的時間地點、和人互動或獨自一人）；第二段要評估兩種方式對消費者的利與弊，並提出自己做得到的具體消費做法。

bands.descriptor_zh: 回應題目的每一項要求，主旨明確；用具體的事例、細節或親身經驗撐起每個重點。
大致回應題目，但有一項要求寫得單薄，或細節偏籠統、說服力不足。

organization.focus_zh: 第一段用對照句逐點比較，最後歸納；第二段先評估利弊，再用自己的經驗帶出做法，結尾提出見解。

bands.descriptor_zh: 兩段分工清楚，各有主題句；句與句、段與段的銜接自然，轉承語用得恰當，篇幅分配合理。

grammar.focus_zh: 描述圖片用現在進行式；評估利弊可用 allow／let＋受詞＋動詞、which 引導的補述子句；提出做法可用 First、Second 列出步驟。

vocabulary.focus_zh: 購物相關字詞要正確（try on、clerk、package、impulse buying、return、discount），避免一直重複 buy、good。

bands.descriptor_zh: 用字精準、貼切，搭配自然，少有重複；拼字與大小寫幾乎全對。

rubric.deductions_zh: 字數明顯不足（少於 100 個單詞）或沒有分成兩段，各扣總分 1 分；兩種情形同時發生只扣 1 分。離題或空白以 0 分計。

checklist_zh: 第一段是逐點比較兩張圖（試穿與詢問、時間地點、互動），而不是兩張圖各寫一段描述
第二段的評估是否兩種方式都有利有弊，而且說明理由
提出的做法是否是自己做得到的具體步驟，並說明效果
有沒有把影響從自己延伸到他人或社會（例如附近的實體店），結尾是否提出見解

model_texts.label: steady
model_texts.text:
The two pictures show two different ways of shopping. In Picture 1, a woman is trying on a jacket in a clothing store. A friendly clerk is helping her and showing her the same jacket in another color. She can touch the clothes and see how they look on her right away. In Picture 2, on the other hand, a young man is shopping on his phone late at night. Near the door, several packages are piled up. He does not need to leave home, but he cannot try anything on before he buys it.
Both ways have advantages and disadvantages. Shopping in a store lets us check the size and quality, so we are less likely to make mistakes. However, it takes time, and the prices are sometimes higher. Online shopping is fast and convenient, but it is easy to buy things we do not need. For example, last year I bought three T-shirts online during a midnight sale. When they arrived, two of them were too small, and I never wore them. Since then, I have followed a simple rule. Before I pay for anything online, I wait for one day and ask myself if I really need it. In this way, I save money and avoid regret. In short, a smart shopper should use both stores and websites wisely.

paragraphs.function_zh: 比較兩張圖：實體店可以試穿、有店員協助；網購不必出門，但買之前無法試穿

model_texts.label: top
model_texts.text:
The two pictures capture two very different shopping experiences. In the first, a customer is standing in front of a mirror in a clothing store, trying on a jacket while a clerk holds up the same style in another color and offers advice. Every decision here is shaped by the texture of the fabric, the reflection in the mirror, and a real conversation, so she knows exactly what she is buying before she pays. The second picture, however, shows a young man alone in a dark room late at night, tapping his phone as a pile of unopened packages sits by the door. For him, shopping has become a quick, anonymous activity available at any hour, yet it is also one in which products exist only as pictures on a screen. In short, the store offers human contact and certainty, whereas the phone offers speed and endless choice.
Each way of shopping has clear benefits as well as hidden costs. Physical stores allow customers to check quality and size, which reduces returns and wasted money, but they demand time and often charge more. Online shopping, by contrast, saves effort and makes price comparison easy; however, tricks such as one-click payment and flash sales encourage impulse buying. I once fell into this trap during a midnight sale, when I ordered four shirts simply because they were discounted. Two did not fit, and the cost of shipping them back was almost as high as the savings, which taught me that convenience can be expensive. Moreover, if everyone shops only online, local stores may close, and neighborhoods will lose not just jobs but also places where people meet. To become a smarter consumer, I now follow a two-step rule. First, I leave any item in my online cart for at least a day, which gives my excitement time to cool down. Second, for clothes and shoes, I try them on in a local shop before deciding where to buy, and if the price difference is small, I support the store that helped me. This habit has cut my spending and made each purchase feel intentional, proving that the real question is not whether to choose stores or screens but how thoughtfully we use both.

paragraphs.function_zh: 比較兩張圖：圖一靠布料觸感、鏡中樣子與真實對話做決定，圖二是深夜獨自滑手機、包裹越堆越多，最後用 whereas 歸納兩者提供的東西
paragraphs.topic_sentence: The two pictures capture two very different shopping experiences.

steady.comment_zh: 第一段對照能否試穿、店員協助與深夜在家下單、堆積包裹；第二段說明兩種方式的利弊，用半夜特價買錯尺寸的經驗帶出「付款前等一天」的具體做法。內容完整但分析較淺，句型以簡單句和 so、but 並列為主，用字正確但平實。

top.comment_zh: 第一段以觸感、鏡子、真人對話對照深夜獨自滑手機與未拆包裹，並歸納為「人際接觸與確定性 vs. 速度與無限選擇」；第二段兩種方式的利弊各有細節（退貨、閃購、一鍵付款），加入對地方商店的社會影響，經驗具體，最後提出兩步驟的消費規則並說明效果。which 補述子句、分號句與 not whether…but how 句型運用純熟。

steady.comment_zh: 第一段針對試穿與網購逐點對照；第二段利弊兼顧，以深夜網購衣服的經驗帶出『等一天再付款』的做法，回應所有要求。句型與用字正確但偏基本。語言無誤。

top.comment_zh: 第一段用鏡子、布料觸感、真人對話對比手機上的圖片、速度與選擇，並歸納；第二段利弊分析深入，有經驗與數字（退貨運費抵掉折扣），兩步驟做法（First／Second）具體，結尾點出重點不是二選一而是如何用心使用。句型流暢多樣，用字精準，語言無誤。
